judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's correctness claims hold: I re-derived every place value, expanded form, comparison, rounded value, the ordering 70425 < 72045 < 72405, the ratio 50000/500 = 100, the carry case 8950 → 9000 and the synthesis item, and all are right; item 12(d) is properly declared manual with a usable grading note. What the assessment misses is that the fast-grading bank on answer_key.pdf answers three of twelve problems with a bare em dash and two more with the number the question already gave. Rows '4. —' and '7. —' are each a problem's ONLY entry — verify.json id 4 is compare([47308, 47380]) expected '<' and id 7 is compare([8090, 8900]) expected '<' — so two problems that were fully verified print exactly what an unchecked manual problem prints, and row 12 opens with the same dash for the verified '>'. Separately, problem 1 asks 'Write 6382 in expanded form' and the bank prints '1. 6382': verify.json id 1 is {type: eval, expr: 'a*1000 + b*100 + c*10 + d', at: {a:6,b:3,c:8,d:2}, expected: 6382}, so the expected value is the number printed in the question and the requested expanded form 6000 + 300 + 80 + 2 is never an expected anywhere. Item 12(a) repeats it ('12. —, 38472, 38000, 38000'). That the correct form is expressible is proved by this task's own study guide, whose try-it check prints '5263 = 5000 + 200 + 60 + 3'. Finally the sheet declares one manual item where it prints at least five open or marked slots: problem 3 'Circle the digit you looked at to decide', problem 4 'Name the place that decided it', problem 6 'Name the digit you looked at', problem 7 'say in one sentence which place Kai should have compared first', problem 11 'explain in one sentence why the thousands digit changed too'.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 5 is the best-designed item on the sheet: an expanded form with the hundreds term deliberately absent (40000 + 3000 + 60 + 5), so the standard form cannot be written without a placeholder zero, and the key names the exact failure — 'Common wrong answer: 4365 — the placeholder zero was left out, and every digit to its left slid one place down in value.'

The synthesis item 12 is built so that both attendances round to the same 38000, which forces the point that rounding destroys precisely the places that separate the two days; part (d) is the one item flagged manual and its grading note tells the adult what to look for ('the idea that rounding removes the very places where the two numbers differ').

Problem 8 (the two 5s in 55505) turns 'how many times greater' into a place-value question rather than a division trick, and the key closes it with the reason it must be a power of ten: 'the two places are two steps apart, and each step to the left multiplies by ten'.
Problem 10's key explains why it is the hard item rather than just solving it: 'a student comparing digit by digit without tracking places will read all three as “the same numbers”.'

root_causes.description: Three of the twelve bank rows lose a verified relation to _fmt's sympify fallback, and on this sheet two of those rows have no other entry, so the bank prints nothing at all for problems 4 and 7. The comparison strand is a quarter of the worksheet and is invisible in the grader's fast-scan column.
evidence: verify.json id 4: compare values [47308, 47380] order relation expected '<'; id 7: compare [8090, 8900] expected '<'; id 12 first entry: compare [38472, 38247] expected '>'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt string branch: sympify then latex, except -> '---'; render_entry returns the same '---' for a manual-only id.

root_causes.description: Both expanded-form items are verified by reassembling the digits into the number the question already prints, so the check is a tautology from the answer's point of view and the delivered bank answers 'write 6382 in expanded form' with '6382'. The verifier has no type whose expected value is a sum-of-place-values string, so the author reached for the arithmetic identity instead.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 1: 'Write 6382 in expanded form.' verify.json id 1 expected 6382; answer_key.pdf bank row '1. 6382'; the key's own worked solution prints '6382 = 6000 + 300 + 80 + 2'.
worksheet.pdf problem 12(a): 'Write Friday's attendance in expanded form.' verify.json id 12 second entry expected 38472; bank row 12 prints 38472.
verify_study_guide.json / study_guide.pdf show the requested form is printable: 'check: 5263 = 5000 + 200 + 60 + 3'.

render_quick_answers.py already warns when ALL banked answers are identical (the equiv-on-a-composition tautology) but has no check for a single row whose expected equals a value printed in the question.

root_causes.description: Only the largest, most obviously open item (12(d)) was declared manual. Five smaller open or marked slots — two 'name the digit/place' answers, one 'circle the digit', and two one-sentence explanations — were treated as covered because the same problem also carries a machine-checkable number.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problems 3, 4, 6, 7 and 11 each print an additional non-numeric instruction; verify.json declares 'manual' exactly once, on id 12.
gate_log.txt gate summary: 'verify-ws MANUAL' — a single manual item for a twelve-problem interleaved sheet.
The prompt requires: 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review.'

improvements.title: Rows 4 and 7 print nothing but an em dash for two fully verified comparisons
improvements.proposed_change: Map relation expecteds to math glyphs in render_quick_answers._fmt before the sympify call, and reserve '---' exclusively for manual-only rows by emitting a distinct marker for values that genuinely cannot be rendered.
improvements.regression_test: Render curr-105's verify.json and assert rows '4.~$<$' and '7.~$<$' and that row 12 begins '12.~$>$, 38472'. All three assertions fail today.
improvements.expected_impact: The comparison strand of this interleaved sheet (a quarter of its items) becomes gradable at a glance instead of requiring the full worked key.

improvements.title: Expanded-form items must verify the expanded form, not the number the question already prints
improvements.proposed_change: Add an answer-form-carrying verification for decomposition items — e.g. an 'equiv' entry whose expected is the literal string '6000 + 300 + 80 + 2' checked for equality against the standard form, with the literal string carried through to the bank verbatim rather than re-sympified. Gate the slot: a problem whose prompt says 'write ... in expanded form' must have an entry whose expected is not equal to a number appearing in the problem's own stem. Extend render_quick_answers.py's existing tautology warning from 'all rows identical' to 'this row's expected also appears as a given in the stem'.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-105's problem 1 (stem contains 6382, verify expected 6382). tests/check_answer_key.py must exit non-zero reporting that problem 1's expected repeats a given. Replacing the entry with an equiv whose expected is '6000 + 300 + 80 + 2' must pass and must render the bank row as '1.~$6000 + 300 + 80 + 2$'.
improvements.expected_impact: Fixes rows 1 and 12 of this key and generalises to every 'write it in another form' item in the suite (prime factorisation, factored form, expanded form), which today all bank the input.
improvements.risk: Comparing a literal string against the stem's numbers will misfire on problems where the answer legitimately equals a given (a check-the-identity item); those should be allowed to declare the repetition explicitly.

improvements.title: Five 'name it / circle it / explain it' slots are recorded as machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the manual-flag lint beyond explanation verbs to marked-representation verbs ('circle', 'mark', 'shade', 'draw', 'ring', 'label') and to short naming answers ('name the place', 'name the digit'), and require a manual entry for each. Where the naming answer is mechanically derivable it may instead be verified as its own slot; what must not happen is the slot going unrecorded.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-105's problems 3, 4, 6, 7 and 11 texts and a verify.json declaring 'manual' only on id 12. The lint must name all five uncovered slots; adding manual (or additional verified) entries for each must make it pass.
improvements.expected_impact: Turns a sheet reporting one open item into one reporting its real six, which is what the prompt asked for and what a parent grading it needs to know.
improvements.risk: More manual entries reduce the machine-verified fraction, which some scoring views treat as a quality signal; the metric should count covered slots, not machine-checked ones.

case_summary: Mathematically clean and pedagogically well-built — the interleaving is real, problem 5's missing hundreds term and problem 12's identical rounded attendances are the two items this focus needs, and the ordering, ratio and carry cases all check out. The ACCEPT stands, but the answer key's fast-grading bank is materially worse than a 4: rows 4 and 7 print nothing but an em dash for two verified '<' comparisons, row 12 opens with a third, and rows 1 and 12 answer 'write it in expanded form' with the number the question already gave, because both expanded-form items are verified by reassembling the digits into that same number. The sheet also declares one manual item while printing at least six open or marked slots. Preserve the placeholder-zero design in problem 5, the synthesis in 12, and the power-of-ten explanation in 8.
